# MAG 7 Daily
> **Five months is the best case for EU iPhone users waiting on Siri AI.**

**What You Need to Know:** Apple's upgraded Siri may stay off European iPhones and iPads for months, and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman calls five months the best case while Apple negotiates the bloc's digital rules. John Ternus is in the design studio several times a week, and a touch-screen OLED MacBook Pro is coming out significantly lighter. CoreWeave says Cognition is already seeing Vera Rubin improve on Blackwell.

### Top News
**EU iPhone and iPad users face a months-long wait for Siri AI: MacRumors**
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman writes in his Power On newsletter that Apple's upgraded Siri AI could remain unavailable in the European Union for several months, and that a delay of around five months would be the absolute best case. He said users there could wait even longer while Apple negotiates compliance with the bloc's digital rules. The upgrade is not available in the EU on iPhone or iPad. Gurman compared the hold with Apple Intelligence's delayed EU rollout. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/05/extended-eu-wait-predicted-for-siri-ai/)

**Ternus takes the design job himself as the OLED MacBook Pro sheds weight: Bloomberg**
Gurman reports that after years without a design chief over both hardware and software design, new chief executive John Ternus has taken that role himself. Since becoming CEO he has worked hands-on in the industrial design and human interface studio several times a week, sometimes more than once a day. Tim Cook typically visited for about an hour once a month at most. The same newsletter says the touch-screen OLED MacBook Pro is significantly lighter after Apple reengineered the interior, miniaturizing parts and rearranging components. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-10-04/apple-s-john-ternus-leads-design-touch-screen-oled-macbook-pro-gets-lighter?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc5MTEyNDY4MiwiZXhwIjoxNzkxNzI5NDgyLCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUTURZVzFWVFRDWkwwMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiJDNEVEQ0FFMUZBMDU0MEJFQTI0QTlGMjExQzFFOTA4MCJ9.PKg1XT__Ut-VKHQIouImouRWeBYPQed6H71pb7IaqJA)

**iPhone Duo puts Focus on the Lock Screen before October orders: MacRumors**
Code explorer pdfu says that when a Focus mode is active, a button above the bottom controls lets you turn it off and back on without leaving the Lock Screen, and the active Focus also appears in the status bar above the clock after unlock. Apple has rebuilt iOS 27 so the interface adapts in real time as the foldable folds, unfolds, and switches between its two displays. Pre-orders open at 5 a.m. Pacific Time on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/05/iphone-duo-focus-modes-easier-toggle-lock-screen/)

**CoreWeave says Vera Rubin is already ahead of Blackwell for Cognition: The Information**
Asked how Vera Rubin is performing for CoreWeave customers, executive vice president Chen Goldberg pointed to Cognition. Goldberg said Cognition has seen an improvement compared with the Blackwell architecture. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/theinformation/status/2106882216206737774)

### Company Desk
**Hon Hai's sales beat tracks continued AI infrastructure spending: Bloomberg**
Nvidia partner Hon Hai Precision Industry reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue. Bloomberg said the figure signals sustained and elevated spending on global AI infrastructure. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-05/nvidia-partner-hon-hai-beats-sales-estimates-due-to-ai-frenzy)

### The Counterpoint
**The EU hold is leverage, and the Mac already has the model: MacRumors**
Gurman reckons Apple is withholding the Siri upgrade to pressure the European Commission, hoping frustrated customers will push for a change in the Commission's approach. EU users already have Siri AI on Mac, so the software is on one Apple platform while iPhone and iPad stay blocked. The open question is whether those talks end inside the five-month best case or run past it. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/05/extended-eu-wait-predicted-for-siri-ai/)

### The Thread: A hundred pauses and a billion-dollar ask
More than 100 data-center moratoriums are being considered across the United States, and that count is now a cloud-build problem, not only a zoning story. AWS chief executive Matt Garman, in a blog post reported by IT Pro, said the build-out is so important geopolitically that there are widespread reports of various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the US about data centers to trick the country into slowing down. He wrote that with any change there will be important questions, but also misinformation and outright lies, and that myths take hold faster in social media and round-the-clock news. Making the wrong choices, he said, could put the country behind, potentially irreparably. The post then names how Amazon wants communities to say yes. Under a program called Built Together, Garman said the company plans to allocate $1 billion over the next five years. How it is spent would depend on the communities, but the money would likely go toward education, job training, energy affordability, and water and energy conservation. He set Amazon next to Microsoft on process: like Microsoft, he said, the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements when seeking approval from government agencies, is providing information as early as possible, and is listening to concerns. On the resource claims, he said US golf courses alone use around 200 times as much water as all of Amazon's data centers put together. He also said the sites are not driving up energy prices and are not emitting huge amounts of pollution via large backup diesel generators. The local case he offered is tax revenue, positive economic impact, large numbers of good jobs, education programs, and other benefits, plus thousands of construction jobs that he said benefit families and local small businesses. Source: [itpro.com](https://www.itpro.com/security/aws-ceo-matt-garman-says-hostile-nations-are-intentionally-seeding-misinformation-in-the-us-about-data-centers-to-trick-us-into-slowing-down) Source: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/aws-ceo-matt-garman-says-data-centers-arent-using-as-much-water-as-claimed-debunks-4-popular-myths-says-there-are-clearly-/articleshow/134689386.cms)

### On the Calendar
Pre-orders for iPhone Duo open at 5 a.m. Pacific Time on Friday, October 16. Availability begins Friday, October 23. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/05/iphone-duo-focus-modes-easier-toggle-lock-screen/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Google will pay about one hundred publishers for what their pages add to AI answers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google is paying roughly one hundred digital publishers based on how much their content contributes to AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini, The Information reports. Google is also preparing to defend a £1.2 billion UK class action over Play charges since 2015. Microsoft is backing a push, with Snowflake and others, to standardize business metrics so AI tools can read company data.

### Top News
**Google Pays 100 Publishers Based on AI Overviews Contributions: The Information**
Google is paying roughly 100 digital publishers based on how much their content contributes to AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini, The Information reports. The payments are tied to that contribution, not to a flat license described in the report. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-paying-100-digital-publishers-ai-overviews?utm_campaign=Editorial&utm_content=Article&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_source=bluesky,threads,twitter)

**Google prepares to defend a £1.2B UK class action over Play charges: Financial Times**
Google is preparing to defend a £1.2 billion UK class action, the Financial Times reported via Techmeme. The claim says Google levied excessive charges on Android apps downloaded from Google Play since 2015. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2106621798720967031)

**Microsoft Backs Effort to Standardize Business Metrics for AI Tools: The Information**
Microsoft is backing an effort with Snowflake and others to standardize business metrics so AI tools can more easily understand company data, The Information reports. The move is an about-face from Microsoft’s earlier effort to protect Fabric from rivals. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/newsletters/applied-ai/microsoft-tears-ai-data-wall?utm_campaign=Editorial&utm_content=Article&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_source=bluesky,threads,twitter)

### Company Desk
**Meta AI 292.1.0 adds email and calendar for glasses owners: MIXED Reality News**
Meta AI reached version 292.1.0 on October 2, on iPhone at 19:25 UTC and on Android the same day, and the build connects the assistant to a user’s email and calendar. Meta’s store copy calls the app the required companion for managing AI glasses, including Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta. Release notes add daily briefings with scheduled tasks and reminders, in-depth research reports, and tools to create presentations, quizzes and workout planners. The description says users can link an Instagram professional account, Meta Ads Manager and Google Workspace so Meta AI can analyze content and ad performance. Voice conversation is quoted at 13 languages, against 39 locales listed for the app; the iOS build is 344 MB and needs iOS 17.2 or newer. The notes describe an assistant on the phone and do not say those features reach the frames. Source: [mixed-news.com](https://mixed-news.com/en/meta-ai-292-1-0-required-companion-app-glasses-email-calendar/)

**Microsoft Rolls Out Excel Canvas, a Copilot Report View That Refreshes as Workbook Data Changes: gHacks**
Microsoft is rolling out Excel Canvas, gHacks reports. It is a Copilot report view that refreshes as workbook data changes. Source: [ghacks.net](https://www.ghacks.net/2026/10/04/microsoft-rolls-out-excel-canvas-a-copilot-report-view-that-refreshes-as-workbook-data-changes/)

### The Counterpoint
**Publisher payouts under a tenth of a percent of ad revenue: The Information**
Some participants in Google’s publisher program say the payouts amount to less than 0.1% of their advertising revenue. That is the figure that decides whether contribution-based pay for AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini is a new market or a rounding error against ads. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-paying-100-digital-publishers-ai-overviews?utm_campaign=Editorial&utm_content=Article&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_source=bluesky,threads,twitter)

### The Thread: Disks Beside a Two-Hundred-Billion Plan
Toshiba plans to double HDD production capacity for AI data centers within FY2027 from its 2025 level, targeting a 30% share by storage capacity, up from about 10%, Nikkei Asia reported. That capacity plan sits next to cash Amazon has already assigned to the buildings those drives are meant to fill. Leverage Shares reported on September 11, 2026, that Amazon’s second-quarter revenue rose 20% year over year for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The same coverage says Amazon posted $200.6 billion in revenue for that quarter. Operating income increased 43% to $27.5 billion, and the operating margin moved from 11.4% to 13.7%. AWS revenue was $42.2 billion, a 36.7% year-over-year increase, while AWS operating income reached $16.6 billion and the segment margin reached 39.4%, according to Fortune. On the second-quarter call, Amazon raised its 2026 cash capital-expenditure plan to $220 billion from $200 billion, Fortune’s transcript reported, aimed largely at AWS and artificial intelligence capacity. A doubled disk line aimed at a 30% capacity share, and a cash plan lifted from $200 billion to $220 billion, are the two scale numbers in front of that build. AWS at $42.2 billion of quarterly revenue, with $16.6 billion of operating income, is the segment those dollars are supposed to keep growing. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2106620532993192263) Source: [ad-hoc-news.de](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/amazon-com-stock-gains-1-33-percent-as-aws-growth-accelerates/70224420)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Apple says affected iPhone 18 Pro Max phones on AT&T must be replaced, not patched.**

**What You Need to Know:** Apple says iPhone 18 Pro Max phones on AT&T that have already lost cellular service cannot be fixed in software and must be replaced. A software update and a carrier-settings update are meant to stop the failure from spreading. Elsewhere, Apple is tightening Mac disk access as Meta gives Muse’s code away, and Google is cutting which Gemini models free and Plus users can open.

### Top News
**Affected iPhone 18 Pro Max phones on AT&T must be replaced: MacRumors**
Apple said on October 2 that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T can lose cellular service, so calls, texts and mobile data stop. Bloomberg reported the bug affects customers who recently upgraded. Apple released iOS 27.0.1 earlier in the week and an AT&T carrier-settings update on October 2, and it wants every iPhone 18 Pro Max user to install the software update now through Settings, General, then Software Update. The carrier-settings update is set to download on its own over the next 14 days; opening Settings, General, then About can trigger it. Apple says phones that have already lost service cannot have that service turned back on with software, and it tells those owners to contact Apple Support or AT&T, or to visit an Apple Store or an AT&T store. Apple says it has seen the failure only on the iPhone 18 Pro Max on AT&T. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/02/apple-statement-on-iphone-18-pro-max-att-issue/)
https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/apple-iphone-18-pro-max-at-t-glitch-requires-device-replacements

**Apple plans tighter full-disk access on the Mac: Bloomberg**
Apple said it plans new privacy controls for Mac users, warning that broad data access for third-party software, including artificial-intelligence agents, is a growing risk, Bloomberg reported. MacStories described the plan as new full-disk access controls on Mac developers. Ars Technica set the move against Meta, writing that Meta says FDA is not sufficient for Muse reading messages and that Apple disagrees. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/apple-to-tighten-mac-data-controls-in-guard-against-ai-agents)
https://www.macstories.net/linked/apple-announces-plan-to-impose-new-full-disk-access-controls-on-mac-developers/
https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/apple-changes-full-disk-access-permissions-to-curb-abuse-from-ai-agents/

**Meta is giving Muse’s code away for other gadgets: TechCrunch**
Meta wants Muse in a television and in a toaster. TechCrunch reported on October 2 that Meta is giving the code away for free so others can build those Muse gadgets. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/02/meta-wants-you-to-build-your-own-muse-gadget/)

**Free and Plus Gemini users lose models in October: XDA**
XDA reported that Google is cutting Gemini model access on the lower tiers in October. On October 9, free users lose Flash and keep only Flash-Lite. Google AI Plus loses Gemini Pro but keeps Flash and Flash-Lite, and Google said Plus subscribers will get an email naming when Pro access ends. AI Pro and Ultra keep Pro, and Google said every other subscription tier is unchanged. Plus subscribers still keep the storage benefits on that tier. Source: [xda-developers.com](https://www.xda-developers.com/google-ai-plus-users-are-losing-access-to-geminis-pro-model-and-its-happening-very-soon/)

**The Netherlands weighs a ban as retailers pull Meta’s AI glasses: Business Insider**
The Netherlands is considering a ban on Meta’s AI glasses, and some retailers have pulled the glasses from shelves, Business Insider reported. A separate report said a Dutch retailer has halted sales. Source: [businessinsider.com](https://www.businessinsider.com/hans-anders-wehkamp-pause-meta-glasses-ray-ban-sales-netherlands-2026-10)
https://finance.biggo.com/news/4b521e3f-947a-45e9-820a-fa62d66bb94b

### Company Desk
**Microsoft delays default Copilot usage billing to December 1: CRN**
Microsoft is delaying the date when usage-based billing becomes the default for Copilot until December 1, CRN reported. The same change adds a spending-cap option. Source: [crn.com](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2026/microsoft-delays-default-copilot-usage-based-billing-to-dec-1-adds-spending-cap-option)

**Amazon’s data-center community plan draws a further backlash: Ars Technica**
Amazon’s one-billion-dollar plan to answer data-center opposition is drawing more backlash, Ars Technica reported. The report said Amazon was praised for ending nondisclosure agreements and slammed for downplaying data-center pollution. Source: [arstechnica.com](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/amazons-1b-plan-to-combat-data-center-backlash-draws-more-backlash/)

### The Counterpoint
**Thousands of complaints against Apple’s “small number”: MacRumors**
Apple’s “small number” sits against thousands of complaints on the Apple Support Community and other platforms, MacRumors reported. U.S. models of the iPhone 18 Pro Max use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem, while models sold in every other country use Apple’s C2 modem, and MacRumors said it is unclear whether that split is a factor. It is also unclear whether Apple will open a service program; MacRumors said it sounds as if Apple Stores will replace affected phones for free. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/02/apple-statement-on-iphone-18-pro-max-att-issue/)

### The Thread: A robot brain at ten billion, with Nvidia and Meta already in the room
FieldAI reportedly raised seven hundred million dollars at a ten-billion-dollar valuation, more than quadrupling a two-billion-dollar valuation in just over a year, Benzinga reported from a Friday Business Insider account. Which venture firm led the round is not clear. A person familiar with the deal told that account FieldAI has added at least thirty-five million dollars in revenue and customer contracts since June, taking the total above one hundred thirty-five million dollars. Founded in 2023, the California company is building what it calls a universal general-purpose brain for humanoid robots, robot dogs, drones and industrial rovers. Last year it secured four hundred five million dollars across two rounds at the two-billion-dollar valuation. Backers then included NVentures, the venture arm of NVIDIA, and Intel Capital, along with Bezos Expeditions, Gates Frontier, Samsung, Khosla Ventures, Temasek, Prysm Capital and Canaan Partners. FieldAI did not immediately respond to Benzinga. Chief executive Ali Agha told Business Insider in June, “We have seen very, very fast growth in the last several months.” The new mark sits near rivals Physical Intelligence, valued at roughly eleven billion dollars, and Skild AI, valued at more than fourteen billion dollars. Meta is already in the same market: it bought humanoid startup Assured Robot Intelligence for an undisclosed sum in May. The valuation is a bet that the brain works in unpredictable settings, not a single task in a controlled room. A Citrini Research report in September, after meetings with robotics labs, engineers and investors in the San Francisco Bay Area, found most humanoid robots still in development, training or tele-operated demonstrations, with real-world deployments closer to pilots than clear return-on-investment cases. That report said basic humanoid locomotion is effectively solved and complex dexterity is not. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62150844/fieldai-700-million-10-billion-valuation-physical-ai)

### On the Calendar
On October 9, 2026, free users of Google Gemini lose access to Flash and keep only Flash-Lite. Source: [xda-developers.com](https://www.xda-developers.com/google-ai-plus-users-are-losing-access-to-geminis-pro-model-and-its-happening-very-soon/)

On December 1, 2026, Microsoft’s usage-based billing becomes the default for Copilot, with a spending-cap option added. Source: [crn.com](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2026/microsoft-delays-default-copilot-usage-based-billing-to-dec-1-adds-spending-cap-option)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Amazon pledged more than one billion dollars to the towns hosting its data centers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Amazon pledged more than one billion dollars over five years to U.S. towns that host its data centers, funding schools, training, and energy and water work as local moratoriums pile up. Google put four of its AI chips on a prototype satellite. Prosecutors charged a California man over restricted Nvidia servers bound for China, and New Mexico is seeking as much as forty billion dollars from Meta after a privacy trial.

### Top News
**Amazon pledges more than $1 billion to data-center towns: GeekWire**
Amazon Web Services said Friday it will spend more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities where it operates data centers, in a program GeekWire reports is called Built Together. The money targets local priorities including education, job training, energy affordability, and water and energy preservation; GeekWire adds free community college and energy upgrades for homes and schools, on top of more than $1 billion Amazon says it has already given those communities over the past three years. Amazon said it invested $276 billion in data centers between 2011 and 2025, with major projects and expansions in Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia, and Mississippi. AWS chief executive Matt Garman said more than 100 data-center moratoriums are being considered, and that “the countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it.” Amazon also said it will stop using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies on data-center projects, install lower-emission backup generators at new sites, publish its energy and water use each year, and pay enough for power to keep local electricity bills from rising. AWS pledged to be water positive across its data centers by 2030, meaning it aims to return more water than it uses, and said it has already reached 75 percent of the progress toward that target. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-pledges-1b-to-data-center-communities-warns-that-local-opposition-threatens-u-s-ai-lead/) https://www.arise.tv/amazon-aws-to-invest-over-1bn-in-us-communities-over-five-years/ https://finimize.com/content/aws-pledges-1-billion-to-ease-data-center-pushback

**Google flies four TPUs on a Project Suncatcher prototype: Google**
Google said it launched a prototype satellite carrying four TPUs into orbit with Planet, on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare. The flight is the first step of Project Suncatcher, a research effort to see whether scalable machine-learning infrastructure can one day run in space. Over the coming weeks Google will collect in-orbit data on how the chips handle physical stress, radiation, and thermal extremes, and use whatever it learns to refine later designs. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Google/status/2105803583648100611) https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-project-suncatcher-facts/?utm_source=tw&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=og

**Prosecutors charge a California man over Nvidia servers sent to China: Bloomberg**
Federal prosecutors arrested a California man on Thursday on charges of smuggling computer servers containing $300 million worth of Nvidia artificial-intelligence chips to China, in violation of U.S. export controls. The Information identifies him as Greg Lui, owner of Earthmade Computer Inc., a privately held firm in the San Gabriel Valley, and says he allegedly worked with conspirators. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-02/man-charged-by-us-with-illegally-shipping-nvidia-chips-to-china) https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/california-man-arrested-smuggling-nvidia-chips-china

**New Mexico seeks up to $40 billion from Meta after a privacy trial: The Business Standard**
New Mexico wants Meta to pay up to $40 billion in penalties after a data-privacy trial, The Business Standard reported. Marketscreener, citing MT Newswires, said Meta faces up to $40 billion in penalties following that trial. Source: [tbsnews.net](https://www.tbsnews.net/world/new-mexico-wants-meta-pay-40-billion-penalties-after-data-privacy-trial-1560216) https://www.marketscreener.com/news/meta-platforms-faces-up-to-40-billion-in-penalties-following-data-privacy-trial-ce785ddadf81f727

**AT&T warns some iPhone 18 Pro Max phones cannot reach 911: MacRumors**
AT&T texted customers that some iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on its network may be unable to complete calls, texts, or data, including to 911, and told them to update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately. MacRumors reports at least thousands of users have described the failure on Apple’s support community, Reddit, and its own forums, with affected phones typically dropping into SOS mode. The U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max is the only new iPhone unveiled last month with a Qualcomm cellular modem; the smaller iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo use Apple’s C2 modem worldwide, as does the iPhone 18 Pro Max in every other country. MacRumors says it is unclear whether that modem split is a contributing factor. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/01/att-acknowledges-iphone-18-pro-max-issues/)

### Company Desk
**Office and science chiefs join a run of Microsoft exits: The Information**
Ryan Roslansky, executive vice president of Office apps, said Thursday he will leave at the end of this year. A day earlier it was Microsoft Science president Peter Lee’s turn, after Office and Windows chief Rajesh Jha and other senior departures over the past few months. The Information says the people leaving are mostly veterans of fifteen years or more, each with their own reasons, and reads the cluster as exits while Microsoft rethinks how it operates around AI. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/microsofts-executive-exodus-foreshadows-business-transition)

### The Counterpoint
**The community check is about a tenth of a percent of this year’s build: GeekWire**
GeekWire’s arithmetic is the hard cut against the pledge. The additional $1 billion over five years works out to about $200 million a year, or about one-tenth of 1 percent of the roughly $220 billion in capital expenses Amazon is projecting this year, largely on data centers and chips — spending GeekWire says is more than the cash the business generates annually. The same report says Microsoft and Google are spending on a similar scale, and that local opposition has become a real limit on the AI buildout. A fund that small does not change the size of the build Garman says moratoriums could stall. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-pledges-1b-to-data-center-communities-warns-that-local-opposition-threatens-u-s-ai-lead/)

### The Thread: Campuses still rising, chips leaving the books
Across five operators, TrendForce’s October tracker finds that most of the capacity it can size is already under construction on the remaining path to 2030, and it reports AWS holding the most gigawatts under construction while Google’s build goes global. The tracker follows major hyperscalers in the United States and China and monitors nearly 2,000 facilities, checking satellite imagery, permit filings, and utility records against its own supply-chain research. Each bar is an operator’s remaining path to a 2030 pipeline target after capacity already online is stripped out: active construction, permitted or planned sites that already have a power figure, and pipeline that has reached neither stage. Permitted or planned sites that cannot yet be sized in megawatts are excluded, so the planned band understates the true total. The count includes self-built campuses, build-to-suit developments, and fully leased colocation, and it excludes shared colocation, cloud regions, and power offtake agreements. Booked delays and unstaged capacity are only a small share of that 2030 window, and where they appear they attach to a few named sites rather than the fleet. Off that construction map, Bloomberg says the Financial Times reported Amazon is exploring a deal to shift about $8 billion of top-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet. On September 30, Synopsys used its 2026 Investor Day in New York to announce multi-year agreements with OpenAI and with Amazon Web Services, and it issued fiscal 2027 revenue and profit forecasts that came in above analysts’ expectations. > **Four Copilot pillars turn Microsoft's work software into an agent layer.**

**What You Need to Know:** Microsoft's largest Copilot update, announced on 25 September, is the same shift: Satya Nadella is pitching Copilot as a new operating system for work, built from Autopilot, Code, Home and Office. Home and Code start through the Frontier programme in the coming weeks. A later private-preview clock covers Autopilot and a new Today view.

### Top News
**Microsoft's largest Copilot update adds Home, Code and Autopilot: Dealroom**
Satya Nadella announced the largest Microsoft Copilot update to date on 25 September 2026 and called Copilot "a new OS for work" spanning every model, form factor and task. Autopilot is a proactive, long-running agent for the enterprise. Code lets people build apps with Copilot hosted inside the company tenant, on the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. Home merges Chat and Cowork into one starting point, and Office puts Word, Excel and PowerPoint fully inside Copilot. Copilot can be invoked in Teams. Today is a proactive view that surfaces the most important information across Microsoft 365. Microsoft says Home and Code begin rolling out through its Frontier programme in the coming weeks, Autopilot expands to private preview at the end of September, and Today enters private preview in October, later coming to Outlook and Teams. Source: [app.dealroom.co](https://app.dealroom.co/news/note/microsoft-unveils-its-biggest-copilot-update-home-code-and-autopilot)

**OpenAI asks a court to strike new Apple evidence in a trade-secrets case: 9to5Mac**

Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/09/25/openai-accuses-apple-of-improperly-adding-new-evidence-to-trade-secrets-case/)

**DeepMind's chief says Gemini 4 should land well before year-end: Trending Topics**
Post-training on Gemini 4 was already in view; what changed is the clock. Koray Kavukcuoglu, head of Google DeepMind, said at The Information's AI Agenda Live Summit that the model should launch "much earlier" than the end of the year, and that Google wants an early version "as soon as possible," then fast improvements, while it is fine-tuned for safety and reliability. Sundar Pichai describes Gemini 4 as a "significantly larger" frontier model focused on coding and autonomous AI agents. In July, DeepMind started what it called its "most ambitious pre-training run yet." Gemini 3.5 Pro, originally announced for I/O in May, never shipped, reportedly because its coding performance fell short. Google instead released cheaper Flash models, Gemini 3.7 Flash in August and Gemini 3.8 Flash in early September. The last true flagship, Gemini 3 Pro, dates to November 2025. TestingCatalog reports Google has been testing Gemini 4 Pro checkpoints under the code name Argon since mid-September; those leaks say a response can run to 256,000 tokens, four times the previous limit, and that the highest reasoning mode took 2.4 to 20 minutes an answer. Source: [trendingtopics.eu](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/gemini-4-rumors-google/)

The lead treats Copilot as a new operating system for work. Windows Latest reports the opposite move on the actual PC operating system: Nadella says "We're building Copilot as a new OS" even as Microsoft strips Copilot from Windows 11. The open question is which surface the agent layer actually lives on once it is no longer a Windows 11 feature. Source: [windowslatest.com](https://www.windowslatest.com/2026/09/26/were-building-copilot-as-a-new-os-says-satya-nadella-even-as-microsoft-strips-it-from-windows-11/)

Ars Technica is the dispatch that puts two of the seven in one frame. On Thursday, Tesla's team was in Sparks, Nevada, for a livestreamed, invite-only factory event that officially launched high-volume production of the Semi. The truck in that account is the 500-mile Semi. The concept first rolled onto a Tesla stage in late 2017, and this production start comes nearly a decade later. Musk has insisted investors think of Tesla as a robotics and autonomous-vehicle company, and he has targeted a $20 trillion valuation, nearly four times the value Ars assigns to Nvidia as market leader. The piece sets a physical limit next to that figure: charging gaps still limit electric trucking as the 500-mile truck moves into volume production. The cross-company fact is not a shared chip order or a joint filing. It is a valuation premise measured against Nvidia, spoken by a chief executive who did not attend his own production launch. Tesla’s insurance entities generated $644.2 million in direct written premiums in the first half of 2026: California $477.8 million, Texas $60.4 million, Nevada $23.3 million, and Maryland $15 million. **Gemini will place the business call, then stay on the line: Notebookcheck**
Google is rolling out “Call for me” as an early preview on Pixel 11, initially only in the United States, so Gemini handles the conversation rather than only dialing. The support page lists product-availability checks, quote requests, reservations, phone menus, and time on hold. Emergency calls, marketing calls, and payments are excluded, and credit card numbers, passwords, and health information must not be shared. Before the call, the app shows the number and the information Gemini will give or request; Gemini then identifies itself as the user’s AI assistant and says the call is recorded. Users can follow a live transcript, listen in, or take over, and afterward get a summary. Notebookcheck reports that transcripts are stored on Google’s servers, audio stays on the device, and neither is used to train Google’s models. The feature is separate from Agentic Calling, which since 2025 has placed certain business calls from Search or AI Mode rather than free-form tasks in the Gemini app. Source: [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Google-puts-Gemini-on-the-phone-AI-handles-calls-for-questions-and-reservations.1408327.0.html)

Source: [simplywall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/media/nasdaq-meta/meta-platforms/news/meta-platforms-meta-draws-42-state-push-to-police-ai-chatbot)

In ongoing lawsuits over alleged harm to teens’ safety and mental health, Meta’s lawyers have argued that certain evidence should be withheld as attorney-client privilege. They pointed to a recently unsealed document, and The Verge reported that employees ordered “attorney/client privilege” hats while those child-safety disclosures were being fought. The New York block lands on a business S&P measured as still expanding, and on a product its own analyst says is not a broad-market insurer. Previous S&P research found Tesla generated $1.37 billion in direct written premiums in 2025, up 40.7% from $970.8 million a year earlier. Tesla-affiliated insurers wrote 75.9% of that business directly in 2025, compared with 32.6% in 2024. California remained the largest market, nearly 70% of 2025 premium volume, at $725 million. Tim Zawacki, head of financial institutions research at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said the purpose “is not to be a competitive source of insurance coverage for a broad segment of the market” and is “to essentially eliminate a point of friction in the Tesla sales process.” He said the shift into affiliated carriers emerged partly because some insurers were reluctant to write electric-vehicle business or charged more because of repair costs and loss severity. DensityAI, founded a year ago by former leaders of Tesla’s Dojo supercomputer program, is in advanced talks to raise hundreds of millions of dollars in a round that would value it at $10 billion, The Information reported, citing two people with knowledge of the discussions. The buy, as those investors were told it, is conditional on performance.

Elon Musk said Colossus 2, an AI computing cluster built by his xAI business, may more than double its current Nvidia chip count by the end of the year, Bloomberg reported. That is a volume target on chips already in the cluster, set against a startup valuation on chips that are still early. They share a calendar. DensityAI’s founders left Tesla’s Dojo effort a year ago and are now describing an Amazon purchase that triggers only if performance requirements are met, while the chips remain years from mass production. Musk’s year-end aim sits on Nvidia parts Colossus 2 already uses, and the scale he named is more than double that current count. For Amazon, the DensityAI clause is optional supply if a new chip qualifies. For Nvidia, Colossus 2 is demand on the parts shipping now. Tesla’s name in the account is the Dojo program those founders left, not the buyer.
